name: Ingushetia
summary_text: Ingushetia is one of the republics explicitly named in the Canadian travel advisory's special-permission requirement (alongside Chechnya and Dagestan) and falls within the North Caucasus zone that the UK Home Office CPIN (June 2025) identifies as the exception to its finding of no state-persecution risk in Russia generally. Isteev of North Caucasus SOS states there is "no safe life for LGBTIQ+ people in the North Caucasus," where private existence can trigger violence, detention, or forced return to families. Like Dagestan, Ingushetia shares the security-and-custom enforcement logic without a documented Chechnya-scale purge infrastructure. The special-access regime limits independent monitoring. Score approximately 0.08 below national (0.12). Equal to Dagestan in evidence quality; well above Chechnya (0.01), which has confirmed secret prisons and extrajudicial killings absent here.

sources.claim_summary: Government of Canada travel advisory for Russia: avoid all travel nationally; terrorist attacks are frequent in the republics of Chechnya, Dagestan and Ingushetia and the neighbouring Stavropol region; visitors must obtain special permission from the Ministry of the Interior to enter certain areas; elevated tensions flagged in the border regions with Georgia, including Kabardino-Balkaria (Mount Elbrus area).

sources.title: “Every year it gets worse” – Protecting LGBTIQ+ people in the North Caucasus - Human Rights House Foundation
sources.claim_summary: Interview with North Caucasus SOS rights defender David Isteev ('Every year it gets worse'): there is 'no safe life for LGBTIQ+ people in the North Caucasus, and even private existence can trigger violence, detention, or forced return to families', worsening year on year.

sources.title: Country policy and information note: sexual orientation and gender identity and expression, June 2025 (accessible) - GOV.UK
sources.claim_summary: UK Home Office Country Policy and Information Note on sexual orientation and gender identity/expression (June 2025): LGBT+ people, including in Chechnya, form a particular social group; there is generally no real risk of state persecution elsewhere in Russia from sexual orientation alone, but people in the North Caucasus, trans people, and public LGBT+ advocates are likely to face treatment amounting to persecution; between 2017 and 2024 Chechen and North Caucasus authorities carried out systematic campaigns against LGBT+ people including abductions, torture and extrajudicial killings, and violence in detention spread beyond the Caucasus after the 2023 'extremist' designation.
